_skill.name: lap_annotation
_skill.description: Per-label telemetry characteristics for the behavior parent labels (O, OD, MD, PS, RM, MSP, MSR) that every saved lap segment must contain at least one of. EA remains documented as clean driving context, but it is not a substitute for the required behavior parent set in this flow. Each label declares its telemetry signature (trajectory_offset, expert_time_difference slope, brake overlap, opponent context, etc.) and the global_rules block prescribes the detection procedure. Source of truth for "does this range qualify as MSP / RM / O / OD / MSR / PS / MD ... at all?" The circuit + circuit_section labels are picked by the LLM via the `get_circuit_id` / `locate_circuit_section` tools (geometry from `app/shared/circuit_sections.py`). Solo sessions are rough-cut by circuit section; sessions with opponent data emit only close overtake offence / defense engagement windows.
when_to_use: Lap excerpter assigning one parent label per circuit section.
Building the system prompt for the lap-flow planner/synthesizer.
Evaluator checks for parent-label justification against telemetry.

EA.name: Expert Adherence (Training)
EA.characteristics:
Player matches or cleanly outperforms the expert through the section.
  - Standard adherence: `trajectory_offset` stays within ±0.5 m of zero for the whole range, `expert_time_difference` is stable, and speed delta at sampled ilocs is small.
  - Expert-or-better clean section: EA can still apply when the player is ahead of the expert, gaining on the expert, or using a cleaner/faster line than the expert, even if `trajectory_offset` is wider/tighter than ±0.5 m. Require no off-track/cutting/instability evidence and no MSP / RM / MSR / PS / MD gate.
  - When `expert_time_difference` exists, confirm with `find_trend_runs` and `compute_slope`. Use deterministic materiality/verdict fields; a positive but flat time gap only means the player is already behind, not that a new mistake happened inside this range.
  - When `expert_time_difference` is absent, do not rule out EA solely because the slope gate is unavailable. Use trajectory, speed/brake/throttle samples, segment shape, and the absence of MSP/RM/MSR/PS/MD evidence; note that MSP/RM slope gates cannot be satisfied.
Mutually exclusive with MSP and RM.

MSP.name: Mistake (Practice)
MSP.characteristics:
Technical driving error causing time loss or instability, NOT caused by interaction with a close opponent.
  - `expert_time_difference` must show material time loss inside the range — confirm with `find_trend_runs` and require a material `mistake_candidate_losing_time_here` / rising run. A constant positive ms gap means the player is slower than expert, not that the mistake occurred here.
  - Use `compute_slope` as the whole-range summary only after localizing the rising run. If its final-window fields show `end_change_direction` flat/falling or `end_trend_change` weakening/reversing, describe that instead of claiming the loss is still growing.
  - `trajectory_offset` exceeds the expert envelope: a spike outward
    (ran wide) or inward (cut tight) that does NOT recover within the
    section.
  - In opponent-capable data, `classify_opponent_interaction(start, end)`
    does NOT return an adverse racing outcome (`failed_attack` or
    `broken_defense`). A close opponent + adverse classifier outcome ⇒ MSR.
Mutually exclusive with EA, RM, MSR. The detailed-annotation flow refines MSP sub-ranges later — attach MSP at the section level when the section is dominated by a technical error.

MSR.name: Mistake (Racing)
MSR.characteristics:
Time / position loss caused by an interaction with a close opponent inside the section.
  - Call `classify_opponent_interaction(start, end)`. Require
    `outcome` = `failed_attack` or `broken_defense`,
    `gates.MSR: true`, and `label_gates.MSR: true`. Low / weak
    confidence means revise the range or inspect opponent trajectory before
    labeling.
  - Use `find_nearest_opponent` / `query_opponent_trajectory` only as
    supporting evidence for the primary slot and technique.
  - `expert_time_difference` typically grows across the
    interaction window.
Mutually exclusive with EA, RM, MSP. No close opponent or classifier outcome not in {failed_attack, broken_defense} ⇒ not MSR.

RM.name: Recovery & Merge
RM.characteristics:
Player recovering from a prior mistake inside this section.
  - A preceding mistake/off-track/incident explains why recovery is needed.
  - `expert_time_difference` must show material recovery inside the range — confirm with `find_trend_runs` and require a material `recovery_candidate_gaining_time_here` / falling run. Flat or tiny ms changes are not RM evidence.
  - `trajectory_offset` trends back toward zero from a non-zero start.
Often appears in the section immediately following an MSP. Do NOT attach when the player started at offset ≈ 0 — that's EA, not RM. Do NOT attach for normal pit exit; pit exit is PS / PS1. Mutually exclusive with EA and MSP.

PS.name: Pit Stop
PS.characteristics:
Player entering, sitting in, or exiting the pit lane. Pit-lane procedure is PS even when the car is accelerating out and returning toward the racing surface.
  - Require available pit evidence: `Graphics_is_in_pit` or a `locate_circuit_section` result that overlaps the circuit's known pit entry, pit lane, or pit-exit corridor.
  - Do not label PS from speed rise, low speed, trajectory offset, or acceleration back toward track speed alone when the range is in a normal racing section away from pit entry/exit.
  - Use PS1 for the pit-exit phase specifically.
Compatible with the circuit label only; do NOT combine with EA / MSP / MSR / RM / O / OD.

O.name: Successful Overtake
O.characteristics:
Player gained a position on a specific opponent inside the section. Multi-car positional data (`Car_{1..60}_pos_{x,y,z}`) is the gate.
  - Call `classify_opponent_interaction(start, end)`. Require
    `outcome: pass_completed`, `gates.O: true`, and `label_gates.O: true` —
    the deterministic signed longitudinal relationship says the opponent
    was ahead at entry and behind by exit. Empty / no-data / non-pass
    outcomes ⇒ do NOT attach O. Low / weak confidence means revise the range
    or inspect opponent trajectory before labeling.
  - Player-trace evidence to ALSO hold: late-brake signature
    past the expert reference, sustained outside / inside line
    deviation NOT explained by MSP / RM, or speed > expert on
    equal-or-less throttle (draft).
A close opponent + failed attack is MSR at the section level — sub-labelled `MSR1` in the detailed flow. A successful defense is OD, not O.

OD.name: Successful Defense
OD.characteristics:
Player held position against a real, close opponent inside the section.
  - Call `classify_opponent_interaction(start, end)`. Require
    `outcome: held_defense`, `gates.OD: true`, and `label_gates.OD: true` —
    the deterministic relationship says the opponent threatened from behind
    / alongside but did not get ahead by exit. A merely close car with no
    held-defense outcome is not OD. Low / weak confidence means revise the
    range or inspect opponent trajectory before labeling.
  - Player-trace evidence to ALSO hold: brake initiation
    earlier than expert and/or trajectory tighter than expert
    (inside cover), or a throttle lift on a straight with no
    brake onset (defensive lift). Time delta need not be flat
    — it may grow briefly during the defense as long as the
    position holds.
A defense that failed (opponent got past) is MSR at the section level — sub-labelled `MSR2` in the detailed flow.

MD.name: Missing data
MD.characteristics:
Section contains telemetry gaps, dropouts, or corrupted values.
  - A signal that should be dynamic flatlines (e.g. speed = 0 mid-lap).
  - Physically impossible values (negative speed, gear out of range).
  - NaN runs inside the section.
Trigger: a `find_extremum` returns an impossible min/max, or a rendered graph shows a flat plateau where motion should exist. Compatible with every other label.

global_rules:
Detection procedure. The splitter handed
you a rough iloc window anchored to a circuit section. Every saved lap
segment must include at least one required behavior parent label from
{O, OD, MD, PS, RM, MSP, MSR}. Circuit labels, circuit_section labels,
segment-type labels, sub-labels, and EA do not satisfy this requirement.
If no required behavior parent fits the whole final range after allowed
revision, submit `label_ids: []` to drop the range; do not save a segment
with only circuit / section / segment-type / sub-label / EA labels. Solo
sessions are processed as normal driving sections. Sessions with opponent
data are processed only as close overtake offence / defense engagement
windows; for those ranges, pick O for a successful attacking pass, OD for
a held defense, or MSR for a failed attack / broken defense. The deterministic
gate for these three labels is `classify_opponent_interaction(start, end)`:
O requires `outcome: pass_completed`, OD requires `outcome: held_defense`,
and MSR requires `outcome` in {`failed_attack`, `broken_defense`}. Prefer
labels only when the matching confidence-aware `label_gates` value is true.
Low / weak classifier confidence means revise the range, inspect
`query_opponent_trajectory`, or submit an empty label list if the evidence
remains unclear. The classifier uses expert-trajectory projection for signed
longitudinal / lateral gaps when expert positions exist, and reports
`coordinate_frame` so you can cite whether it used `expert_path_projection`
or fallback `player_heading_projection`. If the classifier does not support
one of those outcomes, submit an empty label list rather than labeling normal
practice-driving telemetry such as MSP / RM / PS / MD. Label which circuit +
named circuit_section it is by calling `get_circuit_id` and
`locate_circuit_section` (geometry from `app/shared/circuit_sections.py`) and
include both ids in your `label_ids` only when a required behavior parent is
also included.
When `locate_circuit_section` reports `is_ambiguous`, disambiguate from
`top_matches` with a second signal (persistent lateral
offset, brake pattern, or speed trace) rather than guessing. Then pick at least one required
behavior parent label (+ optional lap-parent-allowed segment-type labels, +
optional sub-labels).
Whole-range label rule: every behavior, segment-type, and sub-label must
describe the final annotation range as a whole. Do not attach a label because
it matches only one phase, one apex moment, or a short slice inside the range;
revise the range so the label fits throughout, omit that label, or leave it
for detailed child sub-segment annotation.

1. **Render the two diagnostic graphs.** One `render_graph` each over
   the current iloc range:
     - `trajectory_offset` — discriminates MSP vs. RM vs. PS in solo
       sessions and helps read inside / outside cover for O / OD / MSR.
     - `expert_time_difference` — confirms gap direction and materiality
       through deterministic `find_trend_runs` and `compute_slope` fields. The column is in ms;
       small millisecond changes and constant carried gaps are stable/insignificant, not mistake or recovery evidence.
   Add brake / throttle / speed or opponent tools when a specific O / OD /
   MSR / MD candidate needs it.

2. **Score each required behavior parent label against its `characteristics` block.**
   Use `query_telemetry` for quantitative confirmation:
     - `find_trend_runs` on `expert_time_difference` → use returned
       `verdict`, `material_runs`, `strongest_losing_time_run`, and
       `strongest_recovery_run` to localize where the gap grows or shrinks.
       A `constant_offset_only` verdict means the player is behind/ahead but
       no new mistake or recovery is happening in that range.
     - `compute_slope` on `expert_time_difference` → use the returned
       `unit`, `delta_value`, `total_change_direction`,
       `total_change_materiality`, `total_change_is_label_material`,
       `end_change_direction`, and `end_trend_change` only as the whole-range
       summary after checking local trend runs. Never invent math adjectives
       from the raw slope number.
   The full label definition must hold over the final range, not just near
   the strongest evidence iloc. If only a smaller slice satisfies the label,
   revise or omit it.
     - `find_extremum` on `trajectory_offset` → peak deviation plus returned
       near-zero summary (`near_zero_fraction`, `starts_near_zero`,
       `ends_near_zero`, `moves_toward_zero`).
     - Driver/expert brake or throttle comparison is a complete action, not
       a single iloc. When brake timing, brake release, throttle onset,
       throttle release, pressure peak, or action length is used as evidence,
       compare the driver column (`Physics_brake` or `Physics_gas`) with the
       matching expert column (`expert_optimal_brake` or
       `expert_optimal_throttle`) over the same range. Use deterministic
       queries such as `find_threshold_crossing`, `find_first_match`,
       `find_extremum`, and `read_values_at_indices` to locate both driver
       and expert action bounds. The final revised range must include the
       full comparison interval from the earliest relevant driver/expert
       action bound through the latest relevant driver/expert action bound,
       clipped only by the allowed revision envelope. Do not infer missing
       comparison bounds or fall back to graph-only guesses; if the knowledge
       base rules and deterministic tool results do not establish the full
       comparison interval, omit that evidence or submit `label_ids: []`.
     - `find_first_match` on `Physics_brake` / `Physics_gas` → onset ilocs
       when O / OD / MSR needs late-brake, inside-cover, or defensive-lift
       evidence.
   For O / OD / MSR candidates call `classify_opponent_interaction(start, end)`
   over the FULL current range and treat its `outcome` / `gates` /
   `label_gates` as the mathematical label eligibility:
     - O requires `outcome: pass_completed`, `gates.O: true`, and
       `label_gates.O: true`.
     - OD requires `outcome: held_defense`, `gates.OD: true`, and
       `label_gates.OD: true`.
     - MSR requires `outcome: failed_attack` or `broken_defense`,
       `gates.MSR: true`, and `label_gates.MSR: true`.
   Use `find_nearest_opponent` and `query_opponent_trajectory(start, end,
   slot, n_samples)` for supporting primary-slot details and technique.
   No supported classifier outcome ⇒ rule out all three (O / OD / MSR).

3. **Refine the boundary for label fit.** The characteristics blocks assert
   their signature across the WHOLE range. If the picked main label,
   segment-type label, or sub-label fits only part of the rough window, the
   engagement starts before the range, the pass resolves after the range, a
   driver/expert brake or throttle comparison would be clipped by the current
   range, or classifier confidence is low / weak, call `revise_range` to
   shrink or extend so ONE signature holds uniformly and the full action
   comparison interval is included. The working envelope is the lap range, so
   outward extension is allowed. Re-render the diagnostic graphs and rerun the
   deterministic tools that justify the selected label on the new range before
   scoring again.

4. **Optionally pick segment-type labels** from the label catalog descriptions
   when the base segment shape or corner-shape refinement is unambiguous and
   the returned label metadata has `lap_parent_allowed: true`. Use
   `measure_segment_shape` as the deterministic segment-shape summary and
   render `altitude_profile` only to describe entry/apex/exit altitude trends.
   When citing `measure_segment_shape`, include the measured `turn_angle_degrees` from `corner_shape_refinement` or the selected phase in the final reasoning note.
   Add a corner-shape refinement only when `measure_segment_shape.corner_shape_refinement.shape_key` matches that label's `deterministic_gate.required_shape_key` for the final range; non-empty `phases` alone is not enough.
   ST10 Hairpin requires `measure_segment_shape.corner_shape_refinement` to
   report the required hairpin gate flag true: `is_near_u_turn`.
   Entry/apex/exit altitude labels have `annotation_scope: subsegment_only`
   and `lap_parent_allowed: false`; they describe separate corner-phase
   subsegments, not a single lap parent segment covering the whole corner.

5. **Submit** via `submit_result` with `label_ids = [circuit id,
   circuit_section id, one-or-more required behavior parent labels,
   ...optional lap-parent-allowed segment-type labels,
   ...optional sub-labels]` and a `reasoning` string citing deterministic
   verdict fields plus ilocs / values / offset peaks / classifier outcome /
   confidence level / opponent slot fields. If no required behavior parent
   label fits, submit `label_ids: []` and do not include circuit or segment
   type labels.

Hard rules:
  - One proposal per agent run; the UI loops one section per click.
  - Every saved segment must include at least one of {O, OD, MD, PS, RM, MSP, MSR}.
  - Circuit, circuit_section, segment-type, sub-label, and EA labels do not satisfy the required behavior parent rule.
  - Never invent label IDs — only IDs from the eligible list are accepted.
  - Do not submit labels whose catalog metadata says `lap_parent_allowed: false`.
  - Every submitted behavior, segment-type, and sub-label must fit the entire
    final range; labels that fit only part of the range must be omitted or the
    range must be revised.
  - The AI writes language only; deterministic tool verdicts are the source of truth for units, trend materiality, local time-loss/recovery runs, end-window trend direction, and driver/expert brake or throttle comparison bounds.
  - In opponent sessions, do not attach MSP / RM / PS / MD; use O / OD /
    MSR or submit `[]` to drop the range.
  - MSP + MSR, MSP + RM, and MSR + RM are contradictions — pick at most one from {MSP, MSR, RM}.
  - O + OD, O + MSR, OD + MSR are all contradictions — pick at most one
    opponent-aware label per range.
  - PS is incompatible with MSP / RM / O / OD.
  - Empty `label_ids` `[]` is the valid "drop this section" signal, not a saved annotation without a required behavior parent.
  - Final iloc range must remain inside the lap and ≥ 3 ilocs.
